author: Ash

copy.intro: You've found the Named Collective rhinestone zip you want, then seen the Dusk Rhinestone Zip Hoodie ring up at $210 at US checkout, with free shipping only from $250. So here are the brands that sell hoodies in the same spirit, London drop labels and US streetwear names alike, all available in the US. The closest matches come first, and two cost under $100.

bodies.maniere-de-voir:
Maniere De Voir is the pick if you like Named Collective's zip hoodies but want them cleaner and a little dressier. Start with the Josiane Relaxed Zip Through Hoodie ($125), close to what Named's cheapest zips cost at US checkout.

It runs a US store priced in dollars, so there's no conversion to do. Hoodies go up to the Cropped Suede Hoodie ($260), and the Ollie Unisex Whipstitch Raglan Effect Zip Hoodie ($245) is unisex. Sizes run XXS to XXL. Shipping is free over $250, the same bar as Named, and you get 14 days to return.

The trade-off is the look. There's nothing with rhinestones or bunny ears here. If the sparkle is the point, Broken Planet is the closer match.
bodies.broken-planet:
Broken Planet is another London label built on zip hoodies and limited drops, and it's the closest match on price. The Star Logo Zip-Up Hoodie ($125) is the one to start with, cut boxy and slightly cropped from 540 GSM organic cotton.

Prices are in dollars, and most of its hoodies sit at $125 to $135, with the Deconstructed Star Camo Zip-up at $175. That's right inside what Named charges US buyers. Like Named, it sells in drops, with new pieces every month, so the range changes fast.

The catch is customs. Orders outside the UK pay taxes and duties on delivery, so budget for that on top. Returns close after 14 days, same as Named. If you'd rather skip import fees, White Fox ships US orders from Indiana with tariffs already in the price.
bodies.the-couture-club:
The Couture Club is the Manchester label to try if you want a UK streetwear hoodie at almost Named Collective's pound prices. The Design Department Chest Print Hoodie (£85, about $113) is a good first buy, and the Motion Blurred Zip Through Hoodie (£115, about $153) is its dearest.

Prices are in pounds, so do the conversion before you compare. US orders go by DHL Express for a flat $18 and take two to three working days, quicker than Named's two to five. There's no free-shipping threshold for the US, so it suits one hoodie better than a big order.

Returns stay open for 28 days, double Named's 14, but you pay the postage back. It started in 2015 as a bedroom brand, and sizes run XXS to XXL.
bodies.stussy:
Stüssy is the easy US option, with hoodies priced right inside Named Collective's US range and nothing shipping from London. The Basic Stüssy Hoodie ($130) is the classic, and the Bonded Jersey Zip Hoodie ($195) is the zip to compare with Named's.

It's a California label going back to the early 1980s, born out of surfwear and later picked up by skate and hip-hop crowds. US shipping is $9, or free over $200, a lower bar than Named's $250. Sizes go from XS to XXL.

Returns are tight, though. You get seven days from delivery, half of Named's, and shipping isn't refunded. So check the size chart before you order. If you want more time to decide, Aviator Nation gives you 30 days.
bodies.fear-of-god-essentials:
Fear of God Essentials is for when you want a heavy hoodie without the rhinestones. The Essentials SS26 Classic Hoodie ($150) is the core style to start with.

Hoodies run $150 to $195 in fleece from 380 up to 520 gsm. The Knicks x Barkley Hendricks 90s Hoodie ($195) is the heaviest at 520. Sizes go from XS to XXXL. Shipping is free over $100 in the contiguous US, the lowest bar on this list alongside White Fox.

The big catch is that every Essentials piece is final sale, so nothing can go back. Be sure of your size first. If you want a heavyweight hoodie you can return, Represent gives you 14 days.
bodies.nicce:
Nicce is the cheaper London alternative, and its dearest full-price hoodie costs about what Named Collective's cheapest does. The Nebula Hoodie (£54.99, about $73) is the entry point, and the Mens Zip Through Sweat Hoodie (£74.99, about $100) tops the range.

It was founded in London in 2013, shaped by electronic music and Ibiza club nights, and it made its name on hoodies and joggers. So, as with Named, you can buy the hoodie and the joggers together. It ships worldwide with the cost added at checkout, and you get 14 days to return.

Prices are in pounds, so convert before you compare. Plenty of its hoodies are marked down, so look at the sale section before paying full price.
bodies.evisu:
Evisu is the Japanese denim name to go to for one loud graphic hoodie. The Leopard Multi-Pocket Zip-Up Hoodie ($129) is the cheapest way in, and the Seagull Print Relax Fit Hoodie ($195) carries the brand's famous seagull.

It was founded in Osaka in 1991 and started by hand-painting that seagull onto every pair of jeans, about 14 pairs a day. The US store prices in dollars and works out duties at checkout, so there are no surprises at the door. The range tops out at the Reversible Plaid Fluorescent Daicock Zip-Up Hoodie ($335), pricier than anything Named sells.

Free shipping only starts at $330, the highest bar here, and returns cover 14 days on full-price orders only. So it's better for a single statement piece than a haul.
bodies.represent:
Represent is where to go for heavier, more expensive hoodies from a British label. The Initial Boxy Hoodie ($140) is the starting point, a cropped, boxy cut in 500 gsm brushed-back fleece.

Most of its other hoodies are 480 to 485 gsm, mostly 100% cotton, and prices climb to the Romance Hoodie ($315). It ships US orders from inside the US, for $10 or free over $175. Returns run 14 days, the same as Named, with a $9 charge for the US return label.

Brothers George and Mike Heaton founded it in Manchester in 2011, and it calls itself British luxury streetwear. Sizes run XS to XXL, with XXS on most styles. If you'd rather stay inside Named's $120 to $210, Stüssy fits that range.
bodies.aviator-nation:
Aviator Nation is the pick if the hoodie-and-sweatpants set is what keeps you buying Named Collective, in a sunnier 1970s California style. Hoodies and sweatpants are its foundation, hand-made and broken down for a vintage feel. The La Onda 2025 Relaxed Pullover Hoodie ($120) matches Named's lowest US price.

Most orders ship from its Los Angeles warehouse, so nothing has to clear customs. Returns are generous, with 30 days on full-price pieces and free domestic exchanges. A refund through its label costs $9.50.

Prices climb fast, up to the Vintage Patch Zip Hoodie Relaxed ($450), so sort by price before you scroll. If $120 is already your ceiling, White Fox and Nicce both stay under $100.
bodies.billionaire-boys-club:
Billionaire Boys Club is the one for logo hoodies with a big name behind them. Pharrell Williams and NIGO started it in 2003, and it still mixes streetwear with luxury. The Curve Hoodie ($145) is the cheapest way in, and the NYC OG Logo Hoodie ($150) is the logo piece.

It's a New York brand, so there's no currency to convert, and shipping's free over $200. Returns are open for 14 days, as at Named, refunded as site credit or to your original payment, minus the original shipping.

Prices run up to the New York Made Heavy Weight Hoodie ($390), well past anything Named charges. Sizes are mostly S to XXL, with XS and XXXL on only a few styles, so Named's XS to 3XL covers more people.
bodies.white-fox:
White Fox is the budget pick, with every full-price hoodie between $54.99 and $74.99, well under Named Collective's US prices. The Not Done Yet Zip Up Fitted Hoodie ($54.99) is the cheapest, and the Anything For Love Boxy Zip Front Hoodie ($74.99) gives you a boxier shape.

It's an Australian brand, but US orders ship from its Indianapolis warehouse with taxes and tariffs already in the price. Standard shipping is free over $100, and sizes come in pairs, from 3XS/XXS up to L/XL.

Returns are the catch. You get store credit only, never a refund for a change of mind or the wrong size, within 30 days of ordering. If you want a cheap hoodie you can get your money back on, Nicce refunds within 14 days.

closing.heading: How to choose
closing.body:
Start with your budget. Under $100, White Fox and Nicce are the cheapest, and White Fox ships from inside the US with tariffs included. For Named Collective money, Broken Planet and The Couture Club are the closest UK labels, while Stüssy and Maniere De Voir sell in dollars from US stores.

Then check the returns, because they vary more than the prices. Fear of God Essentials is final sale and Stüssy gives you seven days, but Aviator Nation allows 30 and The Couture Club 28. And if you want something heavier and dearer, Represent and Evisu both go past $300, with Billionaire Boys Club topping out at $390.

faqs.a: In London. It's an independent London collective that designs its hoodies there and sells them through its own store, which charges US shoppers in dollars at checkout.

faqs.q: How long does Named Collective take to ship?
faqs.a: Tracked US delivery takes 2 to 5 days and costs $8, or nothing on orders over $250. UK orders take 2 to 3 days by Royal Mail tracked.
faqs.source_query: how long does named collective take to ship

faqs.a: Yes. It's an independent London label selling through its own store, with tracked delivery to the US and 14 days to return. Exchanges come with a free return label.

faqs.q: Why is Named Collective so expensive?
faqs.a: Its hoodies cost £75 to £130 in the UK and $120 to $210 at US checkout. Most are organic cotton and recycled polyester fleece, decorated with rhinestones, embroidery or detachable faux fur.
